headline: Coarse-grained simulations link membrane, capsid, and nuclear pore mechanics
label: Computational Structural Analysis Tools
summary: Coarse-grained and nanoindentation simulations now probe membrane, viral capsid, and nuclear pore behavior as computational predictions.
synthesis: The dominant thread is computational inference of structural and mechanical behavior from molecular simulation. Coarse-grained MD underlies the endophilin NBAR study, which reports synergistic membrane remodeling and sorting toward negative Gaussian curvature, and the karyopherin study, which describes NTF2 transport receptors entering the nucleoporin meshwork and increasing transport flow. Simulated AFM nanoindentation of CypA-decorated HIV-1 capsids links binding stoichiometry to increased brittleness. What is new is the application of these simulation approaches across membrane, viral capsid, and nuclear pore scales. All findings are computational predictions from preprints, not validated biology.
